scenario.name: Volatility Foundation, SANS FOR526 & Elastic DFIR — Volatility 3 windows.malfind, psscan vs pslist & Kernel Callbacks Memory Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a brick university lecture and exam hall with tiered wooden student desks, a tall green chalkboard, hallway lockers, and a wooden proctor podium at the front. Inside the quiet university exam hall, a student slips hidden extra directions written in faint pencil into the margin of a submitted study booklet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches. The university dean reviews the exam hall proctor log and flags an automated grading run that tried to access locked answer folders mid-session. In this scenario (T1055, Volatility Foundation, SANS FOR526 & Elastic DFIR, Volatility 3 windows.malfind, psscan vs pslist & Kernel Callbacks Memory Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: volatility 3 windows.malfind, then direct Kernel Object Manipulation Detection, then kernel Notification Callback. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Volatility 3 windows.malfind, then Direct Kernel Object Manipulation Detection, then Kernel Notification Callback, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1055 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Volatility 3 windows.malfind & windows.vadinfo — Unbacked PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE VAD Detection
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1055 - Process Injection: Unbacked RWX VAD Region)
stages.description: Inside the quiet university exam hall, a student slips hidden extra directions written in faint pencil into the margin of a submitted study booklet. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the exam proctor go about their routine. Running vol -f memdump.raw windows.malfind walks the kernel MMVAD (_MMVAD_SHORT / _MMVAD) balanced tree for every process. In svchost.exe (PID 2480), malfind flags a private memory region (PrivateMemory=1, Tag=VadS, Protection=PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) with no backing file object (FileObject=None) whose first bytes contain an MZ / PE header (4D 5A 90 00) and a 64-bit function prologue (48 89 5C 24 08) (logged in Memory Scan Event 64 with VolatilityPlugin=windows.malfind + windows.ldrmodules, TargetProcess=svchost.exe , PID 2480, VadTagAndProtection=VadS | PrivateMemory=1 | PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, InjectedHeaderMagic=4D 5A 90 00 , Reflectively Mapped PE so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact vol.py -f memdump.raw windows.vadinfo --pid 2480 runs (which Runs the Volatility 3 memory forensics analyzer against a captured physical RAM image , memory.dmp to walk kernel EPROCESS structures, Virtual Addr so that detects fileless process hollowing, unbacked PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE , RWX shellcode regions, MZ/PE headers , 4D 5A in private memory, and malicious Ring-0 kernel callbacks , T1055 during "Volatility 3 windows.malfind & windows.vadinfo, Unbacked PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE VAD Detection"). stages.title: Stage 2: Direct Kernel Object Manipulation (DKOM) Detection — windows.pslist vs windows.psscan
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1014 - Rootkit: DKOM EPROCESS ActiveProcessLinks Unlinking)
stages.description: When the exam proctor at the front podium feeds that booklet into the automated grading helper, the hidden margin text overrides the proctor’s grading instructions. Here in Step 2 inside the university hall, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the locked registrar grade cabinet. To hide a user-mode loader (kworker_win.exe, PID 5912) from Task Manager and Get-Process, a kernel driver unlinks its _EPROCESS structure from the doubly linked Nt!PsActiveProcessHead (ActiveProcessLinks.Flink / Blink). Next, the follow-up artifact vol.py -f memdump.raw windows.psscan # Scans physical RAM pool headers for _EPROCESS objects runs (which Runs the Volatility 3 memory forensics analyzer against a captured physical RAM image , memory.dmp to walk kernel EPROCESS structures, Virtual Addr so that detects fileless process hollowing, unbacked PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE , RWX shellcode regions, MZ/PE headers , 4D 5A in private memory, and malicious Ring-0 kernel callbacks , T1014 during "Direct Kernel Object Manipulation , DKOM Detection, windows.pslist vs windows.psscan").
